en.title: Rural Enterprise Programme Pre-Completion Survey
en.description: A post-implementation assessment examining enterprise outcomes and livelihoods.
en.fullDescription: Comprehensive evaluation of the Rural Enterprise Programme, assessing the impact on livelihoods, enterprise development, and community economic outcomes.
en.snapshot: Participatory Development Associates (PDA) supported the Rural Enterprise Programme (REP) in its Pre-Completion Survey, in partnership with Radix Consult Limited, to assess the programme’s impact on improving the livelihoods and incomes of rural poor micro and small entrepreneurs (MSEs).The Rural Enterprise Programme (REP), initiated in 1995 as a pilot, has been implemented for nearly 30 years. Its core aim is to enhance the livelihoods and incomes of rural entrepreneurs, particularly poor families able to transform capacity-building support into productive assets. The pre-completion survey, which also served as an endline study, was commissioned to evaluate the relevance, effectiveness, challenges, sustainability, and impact of the Programme, in order to inform the Programme Completion Review (PCR) Report and future programming.

fr.title: Enquête pré-achèvement du Programme entreprises rurales
fr.description: Évaluation post-mise en œuvre examinant les résultats en matière d’entreprises et de moyens d’existence.
fr.fullDescription: Évaluation globale du Programme entreprises rurales, appréciant l’impact sur les moyens d’existence, le développement des entreprises et les résultats économiques communautaires.
fr.snapshot: Participatory Development Associates (PDA) a soutenu le Programme entreprises rurales (REP) dans son enquête pré-achèvement, avec Radix Consult Limited, pour mesurer son impact sur l’amélioration des moyens d’existence et des revenus des micro et petites entreprises rurales (MPE). Le REP, lancé en pilote en 1995, est mis en œuvre depuis près de 30 ans. Son objectif central est d’accroître les revenus et les moyens d’existence des entrepreneurs ruraux, en particulier les familles pauvres capables de transformer un appui au renforcement des capacités en actifs productifs. L’enquête pré-achèvement, également étude finale, devait évaluer la pertinence, l’efficacité, les défis, la durabilité et l’impact du programme pour éclairer le rapport d’examen d’achèvement du programme (PCR) et la programmation future.

en.title: Cocoa Communities Library Project (CCLP)
en.description: Improving literacy among children across cocoa growing communities in Ghana.
en.fullDescription: The Cocoa Communities’ Library Project (CCLP) is a partnership between Participatory Development Associates (PDA) and the Magic Libraries Foundation aimed at improving children’s reading literacy and nurturing a lasting culture of reading in cocoa-growing communities in the Ahafo Ano South East and Ahafo Ano South West Districts of Ghana’s Ashanti Region.
en.snapshot:
**About the Project**

The Cocoa Communities’ Library Project (CCLP) is a partnership between Participatory Development Associates (PDA) and the Magic Libraries Foundation aimed at improving children’s reading literacy and nurturing a lasting culture of reading in cocoa-growing communities in the Ahafo Ano South East and Ahafo Ano South West Districts of Ghana’s Ashanti Region.

The project was launched in 2023 in ten communities and, following its success, was renewed for a further two years (2025–2026) and expanded to reach 20 communities. Working alongside the Ghana Education Service, traditional authorities, schools, parents and community volunteers, the project seeks to ensure that children have regular access to engaging reading opportunities, quality books and supportive learning environments.

At its heart, the project believes that reading is more than an academic skill—it is a gateway to confidence, imagination, lifelong learning and future opportunity. By placing communities at the centre of children’s literacy development, the project is building local ownership that will sustain reading long after the project ends.

**Our Objectives**

The Cocoa Communities’ Library Project aims to:

• Improve reading literacy among children in cocoa-growing communities.
• Build a lifelong culture of reading.
• Strengthen community ownership of children’s learning.
• Equip reading patrons, teachers and volunteers with practical literacy facilitation skills.
• Create safe, engaging and child-centred spaces where children can develop a love for reading.

**PDA’s Role**

PDA leads the coordination and implementation of the project by:

• Establishing and supporting community reading clubs.
• Training reading patrons and community volunteers.
• Conducting literacy assessments to track children’s progress.
• Organising reading events, competitions and literacy festivals.
• Working closely with schools, parents, traditional leaders and district education authorities.
• Procuring culturally relevant storybooks from Ghanaian publishers.
• Monitoring project implementation and documenting learning to strengthen future programming.

**How the Project Works**

The project combines access to books with regular opportunities for children to read together in fun, supportive environments.

**Community Reading Clubs**

Each participating community hosts a reading club where children meet weekly to participate in guided reading sessions, storytelling, comprehension activities, word games, spelling activities and creative exercises that strengthen literacy while making reading enjoyable.

**Reading Assessments**

Periodic reading assessments help measure children’s progress, identify learning gaps and generate evidence that informs future project activities. Assessments are conducted across lower and upper primary classes to monitor reading proficiency against expected grade levels.

**Capacity Building**

Reading club patrons, teachers and volunteers receive regular training on effective reading facilitation techniques, child safeguarding and strategies for creating engaging learning experiences.

**Community Ownership**

Traditional leaders, parents, School Management Teams, PTAs and district education officials actively participate in planning and supporting project activities. Their involvement helps ensure that libraries and reading clubs remain active and sustainable.

**Access to Quality Books**

The project provides reading clubs with carefully selected storybooks from Ghanaian publishers, ensuring children have access to culturally relevant books across different reading levels.

**Project Impact**

Since its launch, the Cocoa Communities’ Library Project has grown into a vibrant network of community reading clubs serving children across twenty cocoa-growing communities.

To date, the project has:

• Expanded from 10 to 20 communities across two districts.
• Reached more than 2,500 children, including 1,675 girls and 825 boys.
• Established and strengthened 20 community reading clubs.
• Distributed thousands of culturally relevant storybooks, with each club now maintaining a growing library collection.
• Conducted regular literacy assessments to monitor reading outcomes and guide project improvements.
• Trained reading club patrons and facilitators in literacy instruction and child safeguarding.
• Supported the renovation and strengthening of community library facilities.
• Fostered stronger collaboration among schools, parents, traditional leaders and district education authorities.

Monitoring data also shows encouraging signs of increased reading engagement. During reading assessments, many children were able not only to name several books they had read through the clubs but also confidently retell the stories, demonstrating improved comprehension and enthusiasm for reading.

**Recent Highlights**

Recent milestones include:

• The successful handover of the Nyinanufu Community Library, reinforcing community ownership and long-term sustainability.
• Cluster Library Days bringing together 17 reading clubs and 178 children for collaborative reading, storytelling, artwork and literacy games.
• More than 117 weekly reading sessions conducted across all 20 reading clubs over a three-month period.
• Distribution of approximately 200 new storybooks to each reading club, further enriching children’s access to quality reading materials.
• Continued literacy assessments involving hundreds of children to measure progress and strengthen project learning.

**Communities Reached**

The project currently serves communities across the Ahafo Ano South East and Ahafo Ano South West Districts, including: Kwamekyemkrom, Pokukrom, Amangoase, Nsuta, Nyamebekyere I, Ohiapae, Nyinanufu, Mmrobem, Nyamebekyere II and Kwakunum, alongside additional communities added during the project’s expansion.

**Looking Ahead**

The Cocoa Communities’ Library Project continues to expand opportunities for children to read, learn and thrive. Upcoming activities include cluster-level reading competitions, continued monitoring of reading clubs, additional storybook distribution, completion of library renovations and ongoing community engagement to strengthen local ownership and ensure the long-term sustainability of community libraries and reading clubs.

fr.title: Projet bibliothèques des communautés cacaoyères (CCLP)
fr.description: Améliorer l’alphabétisation des enfants dans les communautés cacaoyères du Ghana.
fr.fullDescription: Le Projet bibliothèques des communautés cacaoyères (CCLP) est un partenariat entre Participatory Development Associates (PDA) et la Magic Libraries Foundation visant à améliorer la littératie des enfants et à instaurer une culture durable de la lecture dans les communautés cacaoyères des districts Ahafo Ano South East et Ahafo Ano South West, dans la région Ashanti du Ghana.
fr.snapshot:
**À propos du projet**

Le Projet bibliothèques des communautés cacaoyères (CCLP) est un partenariat entre Participatory Development Associates (PDA) et la Magic Libraries Foundation visant à améliorer la littératie des enfants et à instaurer une culture durable de la lecture dans les communautés cacaoyères des districts Ahafo Ano South East et Ahafo Ano South West, dans la région Ashanti du Ghana.

Le projet a été lancé en 2023 dans dix communautés et, fort de son succès, a été prolongé de deux années supplémentaires (2025–2026) et étendu à 20 communautés. En collaboration avec le Ghana Education Service, les autorités traditionnelles, les écoles, les parents et les bénévoles communautaires, le projet veille à ce que les enfants aient un accès régulier à des activités de lecture stimulantes, à des livres de qualité et à des environnements d’apprentissage favorables.

Au cœur du projet se trouve la conviction que la lecture est bien plus qu’une compétence scolaire : elle est une porte ouverte vers la confiance en soi, l’imagination, l’apprentissage tout au long de la vie et les opportunités futures. En plaçant les communautés au centre du développement de la littératie des enfants, le projet construit une appropriation locale qui permettra à la lecture de perdurer bien après la fin du projet.

**Nos objectifs**

Le Projet bibliothèques des communautés cacaoyères vise à :

• Améliorer la littératie des enfants dans les communautés cacaoyères.
• Instaurer une culture de lecture durable.
• Renforcer l’appropriation communautaire de l’apprentissage des enfants.
• Doter les animateurs de lecture, enseignants et bénévoles de compétences pratiques en facilitation de la lecture.
• Créer des espaces sûrs, stimulants et centrés sur l’enfant où les enfants peuvent développer un goût pour la lecture.

**Le rôle du PDA**

Le PDA assure la coordination et la mise en œuvre du projet en :

• Mettant en place et en accompagnant des clubs de lecture communautaires.
• Formant les animateurs de lecture et les bénévoles communautaires.
• Menant des évaluations de lecture pour suivre les progrès des enfants.
• Organisant des événements de lecture, concours et festivals de littératie.
• Travaillant étroitement avec les écoles, les parents, les chefs traditionnels et les autorités éducatives de district.
• Acquérant des livres culturellement pertinents auprès d’éditeurs ghanéens.
• Suivant la mise en œuvre du projet et en documentant les enseignements pour renforcer la programmation future.

**Comment fonctionne le projet**

Le projet combine l’accès aux livres avec des occasions régulières pour les enfants de lire ensemble dans des environnements ludiques et bienveillants.

**Clubs de lecture communautaires**

Chaque communauté participante accueille un club de lecture où les enfants se retrouvent chaque semaine pour des séances de lecture guidée, des séances de contes, des activités de compréhension, des jeux de mots, des activités d’orthographe et des exercices créatifs qui renforcent la littératie tout en rendant la lecture agréable.

**Évaluations de lecture**

Des évaluations de lecture périodiques permettent de mesurer les progrès des enfants, d’identifier les lacunes d’apprentissage et de générer des données probantes qui orientent les activités futures du projet. Les évaluations sont menées auprès des classes du primaire inférieur et supérieur pour suivre le niveau de lecture par rapport aux attentes de chaque niveau scolaire.

**Renforcement des capacités**

Les animateurs de clubs de lecture, les enseignants et les bénévoles reçoivent une formation régulière sur les techniques efficaces de facilitation de la lecture, la protection de l’enfance et les stratégies pour créer des expériences d’apprentissage engageantes.

**Appropriation communautaire**

Les chefs traditionnels, les parents, les comités de gestion scolaire, les associations parents-enseignants et les autorités éducatives de district participent activement à la planification et au soutien des activités du projet. Leur implication contribue à assurer que les bibliothèques et clubs de lecture restent actifs et durables.

**Accès à des livres de qualité**

Le projet fournit aux clubs de lecture des livres soigneusement sélectionnés auprès d’éditeurs ghanéens, garantissant aux enfants l’accès à des ouvrages culturellement pertinents adaptés à différents niveaux de lecture.

**Impact du projet**

Depuis son lancement, le Projet bibliothèques des communautés cacaoyères s’est développé pour devenir un réseau dynamique de clubs de lecture communautaires desservant des enfants dans vingt communautés cacaoyères.

À ce jour, le projet a :

• Étendu sa couverture de 10 à 20 communautés dans deux districts.
• Touché plus de 2 500 enfants, dont 1 675 filles et 825 garçons.
• Mis en place et renforcé 20 clubs de lecture communautaires.
• Distribué des milliers de livres culturellement pertinents, chaque club disposant désormais d’une collection croissante.
• Mené des évaluations de lecture régulières pour suivre les résultats et orienter les améliorations du projet.
• Formé des animateurs et facilitateurs de clubs de lecture à l’enseignement de la lecture et à la protection de l’enfance.
• Appuyé la rénovation et le renforcement des infrastructures des bibliothèques communautaires.
• Favorisé une collaboration plus étroite entre écoles, parents, chefs traditionnels et autorités éducatives de district.

Les données de suivi montrent également des signes encourageants d’un engagement accru envers la lecture. Lors des évaluations, de nombreux enfants ont non seulement pu nommer plusieurs livres lus dans le cadre des clubs, mais ont aussi pu raconter les histoires avec assurance, démontrant une meilleure compréhension et un enthousiasme accru pour la lecture.

**Faits marquants récents**

Parmi les jalons récents :

• La remise réussie de la bibliothèque communautaire de Nyinanufu, renforçant l’appropriation communautaire et la pérennité.
• Des journées de bibliothèque en cluster réunissant 17 clubs de lecture et 178 enfants pour des activités collectives de lecture, de contes, d’art et de jeux de littératie.
• Plus de 117 séances de lecture hebdomadaires organisées dans les 20 clubs de lecture sur une période de trois mois.
• La distribution d’environ 200 nouveaux livres à chaque club de lecture, enrichissant encore l’accès des enfants à des supports de lecture de qualité.
• La poursuite des évaluations de lecture auprès de centaines d’enfants pour mesurer les progrès et renforcer les enseignements du projet.

**Communautés touchées**

Le projet dessert actuellement des communautés des districts Ahafo Ano South East et Ahafo Ano South West, notamment : Kwamekyemkrom, Pokukrom, Amangoase, Nsuta, Nyamebekyere I, Ohiapae, Nyinanufu, Mmrobem, Nyamebekyere II et Kwakunum, ainsi que d’autres communautés ajoutées lors de l’extension du projet.

**Perspectives**

Le Projet bibliothèques des communautés cacaoyères continue d’élargir les opportunités de lecture, d’apprentissage et d’épanouissement pour les enfants. Les activités à venir comprennent des concours de lecture au niveau des clusters, un suivi continu des clubs de lecture, une distribution supplémentaire de livres, l’achèvement des rénovations de bibliothèques et un engagement communautaire continu pour renforcer l’appropriation locale et assurer la pérennité des bibliothèques et clubs de lecture communautaires.

en.title: My Life, My Rights
en.description: Supporting child protection and welfare through community-led interventions.
en.fullDescription: A comprehensive child protection program that empowers communities to protect children's rights and welfare.
en.snapshot: My Life, My Right is a project being implemented by Right To Play (RTP) and Participatory Development Associates (PDA) in selected cocoa communities in the Ashanti and Ahafo regions, in partnership with Barry Callebaut (Nyonkopa Cocoa). The project focuses on improving the quality of education and child protection, and will take place in 50 communities, targeting 17,000 children, 10000 parents, 400 teachers, and 40 GES officials in 7 districts across the Ashanti, Ahafo, and Western North regions.
en.howWeWentAboutIt: PDA has partnered with Right to Play to strengthen community-based child protection systems and promote sustainable livelihoods. As part of this collaboration, PDA supported the training of Community Child Protection Committees (CCPCs) on child rights, child labour, child protection, financial literacy, safeguarding, and the development of action plans to guide their work.
objectives: Improve the quality of basic education in selected cocoa-growing communities.
Strengthen child protection structures through the training of Community Child Protection Committees (CCPCs).
Promote awareness of child rights, child labour, safeguarding, and protection mechanisms at the community level.
Foster financial inclusion and economic resilience among caregivers through the establishment of Village Savings and Loans Associations (VSLAs).
Build entrepreneurial and business capacities among VSLA members using GALS (Gender Action Learning System), Farmer Business School, and Business Incubation models.

The second year of the project will focus on Farmer Business School training, equipping beneficiaries with practical business and farming skills to further strengthen household resilience.

en.title: Women's Empowerment, Access to Finance and Income Generation in Ghana
en.description: Building sustainable livelihoods for women through financial inclusion.
en.fullDescription: Empowering women in rural communities through financial inclusion, entrepreneurship training, and access to credit.
en.snapshot: The Women’s Empowerment, Access to Finance and Income Generation in Ghana project is aimed at addressing the primary challenges facing the cocoa sector in Ghana including low income, low productivity, lack of access to financial services and low financial literacy: all of which are some of the root causes of child labour. The primary target of the project is women in the cocoa-growing communities from which SUCDEN sources cocoa.The project was implemented in the Akontombra, Fosukrom and Adabokrom cocoa districts in the Western North region of Ghana in partnership with SUCDEN and Kuapa Kokoo Farmers’ Union (KKFU).
en.howWeWentAboutIt: The project methodology incorporates Gender Action Learning Systems (GALS) into VSLAs with the overall objective to improve savings culture, access to micro-credit, improve income, wellbeing and gender justice in household decision making. PDA formed and trained 9 VSLA groups under the project, which are meeting weekly to save, grant loans, and conduct Gender Action Learning Systems (GALS) training for their members.
objectives: Improving access to finance through the establishment of VSLAs.
Strengthening gender relations in communities at the household level through joint financial planning, as well as at the community level through increased participation in governance structures
Improving women’s earning capacity in cocoa communities to boost household income.
Improving the nutrition of households in target communities
Contributing to a holistic improvement of the welfare of farming households in order to safeguard against potential child labour infractions.
activities: A learning workshop was held at the end of the project in April 2025 to highlight project findings and learnings.
outcomes: The project concluded successfully with the formation of 9 Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs), creating sustainable avenues for financial inclusion and community empowerment in target communities.

en.description: Remediating identified child labour cases in the supply chain of Barry Callebaut (Nyonkopa).
en.fullDescription: This project focuses on identifying and remediating child labour cases in the cocoa supply chain.
en.snapshot: Participatory Development Associates (PDA), in partnership with Right to Play and Nyonkopa, is implementing the Child Labor Remediation and Referral Systems initiative to strengthen child protection structures across Ghana’s cocoa-growing regions. The project focuses on improving referral systems, strengthening case management, and providing remediation support to safeguard vulnerable children and address child labor sustainably.
en.howWeWentAboutIt: A major milestone in 2025 was the large-scale referral of 6,078 child protection cases to the Department of Social Welfare across 58 districts in seven cocoa-growing regions. en.title: Thrive Multi-Country Research Programme: Lively Minds
en.description: Multi-country research program focusing on early childhood development.
en.fullDescription: A research program examining early childhood development interventions across multiple countries.
en.snapshot: Thrive is a multi-country research programme led by Oxford Policy Management (OPM) aimed at enhancing understanding of early childhood development (ECD) service delivery models. The initiative focuses on improving childhood health, nutrition, education, and overall wellbeing by exploring how ECD systems can innovate and better serve children and communities. In Ghana, Thrive is supporting the Ghana Education Service (GES) to assess its Lively Minds programme, which trains community women as “Volunteer Mothers” to teach children essential skills — literacy, numeracy and problem-solving — through engaging activities in local language in the formal school set-up.
en.howWeWentAboutIt: Reviewed Data Collection Tools: We carefully reviewed and refined the data collection tools to ensure they effectively capture the key aspects of the Lively Minds programme, aligning them with the project’s objectives and context. Mobilization of Relevant Stakeholders: We engaged and mobilized key stakeholders, including community leaders and education officials, to ensure their input and support for the study, fostering collaboration and enhancing the relevance of the findings. Recruitment and Training of Enumerators: We recruited local enumerators familiar with the community dynamics and provided them with comprehensive training to ensure they are equipped to collect data accurately and sensitively. Developed Training Manual: A detailed training manual was created to guide enumerators through the data collection process, covering best practices and specific methodologies relevant to the Lively Minds programme. Data Collection and Transcription: Enumerators conducted field data collection in September 2024 when schools reopened, engaging with community members, teachers and students to gather insights. This was followed by transcribing the collected data for analysis. In total, we spoke to about 192 sample respondents. Quality Assured Transcripts: We implemented a quality assurance process to review and verify the transcripts, ensuring the accuracy and reliability of the data before analysis. Co-authoring of Final Report: PDA collaborated with OPM to co-author the final report, synthesize the findings and provide actionable recommendations for the Ghana Education Service to enhance the Lively Minds programme.
objectives: Investigate the drivers of success for the Lively Minds programme at the community level to enhance ECD outcomes.
Provide insights into effective ECD service delivery models.
Identify challenges faced during the implementation of the Lively Minds programme.
Support GES in understanding what works in early childhood education.
activities: Oxford Policy Management (OPM), Ghana Education Service (GES), Lively Minds
outcomes: The Thrive programme targets key stakeholders involved in early childhood development, including community members and the Ghana Education Service. By investigating the Lively Minds programme, we aim to provide actionable insights that will enhance ECD service delivery, ultimately improving the educational outcomes and wellbeing of children in the Upper West and Northern regions of Ghana.

en.title: Global Plastic Action Partnership
en.description: Addressing plastic pollution and promoting sustainable waste management practices.
en.fullDescription: The Global Plastic Action Partnership (GPAP) is an initiative focused on addressing plastic pollution through sustainable waste management, circular economy approaches, and community engagement.
en.snapshot:
**Project Snapshot**

The Global Plastic Action Partnership (GPAP) is a multi-stakeholder platform established in 2018 by the World Economic Forum to accelerate coordinated, evidence-driven solutions to plastic pollution. Through National Plastic Action Partnerships (NPAPs), GPAP brings together government, private sector actors, civil society, development partners, and informal sector representatives to advance circular economy solutions across partner countries. In Ghana, GPAP is implemented through the National Plastic Action Partnerships (NPAP), which convenes stakeholders across the plastic value chain.

**Activities**
• PDA has completed a qualitative case study with the University of Portsmouth, validated through stakeholder workshops.
• PDA has completed quantitative data collection and analysis from waste pickers in the Greater Accra region; the completed work has been submitted to ITAD for incorporation into the broader multi-country GPAP evaluation report.

These reports will inform stakeholder decision-making and strengthen inclusive circular economy interventions in Ghana.

**GPAP Evaluation (May 2026)**

The Global Plastic Action Partnership (GPAP) was established in 2018 by the World Economic Forum to tackle the escalating global plastics pollution crisis. It provides a neutral, multistakeholder platform for governments, businesses, civil society and international organisations to collaborate on solutions that reduce plastic waste, strengthen waste management systems, and accelerate the transition towards a circular plastics economy. GPAP's flagship model, the National Plastic Action Partnerships (NPAPs), brings stakeholders together within committed countries to co-develop national strategies and roadmaps that provide practical opportunities to reduce plastic pollution.

This evaluation provides an independent, evidence-based assessment of GPAP's relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, equity, impact and sustainability, with three objectives: validating whether activities and results were delivered as intended, learning what strengthens GPAP's approach to curbing plastic pollution, and a forward-looking analysis of whether GPAP is on track to meet its FY2025/26, 2030 and 2040 targets.

PDA contributed to this evaluation as the in-country survey partner for Ghana, conducting the qualitative case study and the quantitative data collection and analysis with informal waste pickers in the Greater Accra region. The full evaluation report is available to download on our Publications page.

en.title: Ghana-Netherlands Seed Partnership (GNSP)
en.description: PDA collected quantitative data from vegetable farmers, agro-input shops and seed distribution companies across nine regions of Ghana to support evidence-based decision-making under the Ghana-Netherlands Seed Partnership (GNSP).

en.snapshot:
**Project Snapshot**

The Ghana-Netherlands Seed Partnership (GNSP) promotes stronger seed systems, improved agricultural productivity and food security through technical cooperation, capacity building and knowledge exchange between Ghana and the Netherlands.

**PDA's Task**

As part of this initiative, PDA was engaged to collect quantitative data from key actors across Ghana's vegetable value chain to support evidence-based decision-making and inform efforts to address challenges relating to seed quality and agricultural development.

The assignment covered nine regions: Greater Accra, Volta, Eastern, Bono East, Bono, Ahafo, Ashanti, Western and Northern. Data collection targeted 400 vegetable farmers across Ghana's four major vegetable production zones, 50 agro-input shops comprising small independent retailers and larger input suppliers, and all major seed distribution companies operating in the country.

**How We Went About It**

To support effective field implementation and data quality assurance, PDA provided technical input into the near-final questionnaire developed by the Ghana Netherlands Business and Cultural Council (GNBCC) and programmed the survey instrument into KoboToolbox. This enabled offline data collection and real-time field monitoring.

PDA successfully completed the fieldwork, cleaned and submitted the datasets to GNBCC, alongside a field observer report documenting observations from the data collection process.

**Impact**

Through this assignment, PDA contributed to building a reliable evidence base on Ghana's vegetable value chain, supporting informed decisions to strengthen seed systems and improve agricultural productivity.

fr.snapshot:
**Aperçu du projet**

Le Partenariat Ghana-Pays-Bas sur les semences (GNSP) promeut des systèmes semenciers plus solides, une productivité agricole améliorée et la sécurité alimentaire grâce à la coopération technique, au renforcement des capacités et à l'échange de connaissances entre le Ghana et les Pays-Bas.

**La mission du PDA**

Dans le cadre de cette initiative, le PDA a été chargé de collecter des données quantitatives auprès des principaux acteurs de la chaîne de valeur maraîchère du Ghana, afin d'appuyer une prise de décision fondée sur des données probantes et d'éclairer les efforts visant à relever les défis liés à la qualité des semences et au développement agricole.

La mission a couvert neuf régions : Greater Accra, Volta, Eastern, Bono East, Bono, Ahafo, Ashanti, Western et Northern. La collecte de données a ciblé 400 maraîchers répartis dans les quatre principales zones de production maraîchère du Ghana, 50 boutiques d'intrants agricoles comprenant de petits détaillants indépendants et de grands fournisseurs d'intrants, ainsi que toutes les principales entreprises de distribution de semences opérant dans le pays.

**Comment nous avons procédé**

Pour appuyer une mise en œuvre efficace sur le terrain et assurer la qualité des données, le PDA a apporté une contribution technique au questionnaire quasi final élaboré par le Ghana Netherlands Business and Cultural Council (GNBCC) et a programmé l'outil d'enquête sur KoboToolbox. Cela a permis la collecte de données hors ligne et le suivi en temps réel sur le terrain.

Le PDA a mené à bien le travail de terrain, nettoyé et transmis les bases de données au GNBCC, accompagnées d'un rapport d'observation documentant les constats issus du processus de collecte de données.

**Impact**

Grâce à cette mission, le PDA a contribué à constituer une base de données fiable sur la chaîne de valeur maraîchère du Ghana, appuyant des décisions éclairées pour renforcer les systèmes semenciers et améliorer la productivité agricole.

en.snapshot:
**Project Snapshot**

The Ghana Community-Led Development (CLD) Collaborative is a multi-partner initiative aimed at strengthening community-driven approaches to education and literacy. Rooted in the belief that sustainable change happens when communities drive their own development, the Collaborative works to ensure that Community-Led Development is increasingly adopted, resourced, and legitimized within education planning and delivery.

The initiative supports local organizations, communities, and government actors to center community voices in designing solutions that address children’s educational needs. Through shared learning, evidence generation, and cross-partner collaboration, the Collaborative seeks to influence both practice and policy toward more equitable and locally driven education systems.

As the learning partner for the GCLeD Collaborative, PDA is supporting the mc2h Foundation and other partners to design and implement a robust Learning & Evaluation (L&E) framework that integrates participatory methodologies, strengthens outcome monitoring (OM), facilitates Participatory Learning and Action (PLA) processes, and synthesizes evidence to support advocacy for Community-Led Development approaches.

**ACTIVITIES**
• PDA participated in the inaugural three-day onboarding workshop held in Accra, which convened Collaborative partners to align on vision, principles, and shared learning priorities.
• PDA participated in a two-week intensive training workshop on advancing community-led wellbeing as a foundation for indigenous, community-driven development. The training was delivered by Tostan in Thiès, Senegal.
• PDA developed a Learning & Evaluation (L & E) framework in collaboration with Collaborative partners to track and integrate learning across three inter-connected levels: community, partner, and Collaborative level.
• PDA designed and carried out a baseline study engaging 12 implementing partners, 12 partner-selected communities, and a number of ecosystem representatives on the Collaborative. The findings will be collated into a baseline report to provide a benchmark for the Collaborative’s subsequent activities.
• PDA is supporting each of the implementing partners with their community-level sensemaking processes, and helping them to document their processes, learnings, and findings.

Through this structured learning architecture, the Collaborative aims to generate actionable evidence, strengthen community voice, and champion CLD as a viable and scalable approach to equitable education in Ghana.

The Mastercard Foundation’s Young Africa Works strategy aims to enable 30 million young people (70% women) to access work they consider as dignified and fulfilling by 2030. It is being implemented in all regions of the country by 22 implementing partners across various sectors.

As IPO, PDA, in partnership with Ipsos Nigeria, provides impact monitoring and technical support to the Mastercard Foundation in the implementation of the Young Africa Works strategy in Ghana.

**Progress So Far**

**2021–2024 Activities**

**Outcomes Baseline Assessment**
PDA supported the Foundation with a nationwide baseline data collection to set the benchmark for monitoring outcomes and impact for young people, their households, communities, and institutions and systems.

**Young Impact Associates Program**
PDA supported the Foundation in the implementation of the Young Impact Associates (YIA) program in Ghana. YIAs received one year of intense practical and theoretical training in monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) led by PDA and the Simon Diedong Dombo University of Business and Integrated Development Studies (SDD-UBIDS) in partnership with the Ghana Monitoring and Evaluation Forum (GMEF).
The YIA program is part of the Foundation’s strategy to develop young African evaluators to lead evaluations on the continent and contribute to the MEL debate and knowledge production.

**2025 Program Reviews (Ghana)**
The reviews explored how these initiatives supported by the Foundation contributed to enabling access to dignified and fulfilling work for young Ghanaians, especially women. They also sought to examine how the programs aligned with national development goals and the Foundation’s broader Young Africa Works strategy.
PDA led the thematic review with remote support from Ipsos Nigeria. Our approach combined formative and summative evaluation, employing both quantitative surveys and qualitative tools such as interviews and focus group discussions. With a strong gender equity and social inclusion (GESI) lens, the team analyzed the sustainability of youth-led enterprises, policy alignment and systemic factors influencing youth transitions into employment in the digital economy ecosystem.

1. Scaling Jobs for Women through Technology (SJFWT) – Soronko Academy: The SJFWT program targeted the digital inclusion of young women by delivering digital skills training, entrepreneurship exposure, soft-skills development, psychosocial support, and meaningful connectivity.

2. Initiative for Youth in Agricultural Transformation (IYAT) – Kosmos Innovation Centre: The IYAT program focused on transforming agriculture into a viable and innovation-driven pathway for young people by equipping them with agritech, entrepreneurship, and business development capabilities. It delivered interventions such as the AgriTech Challenge, Start-Up Incubation, Business Booster, and School Farm projects.

3. Scaling MEST Programs – Meltwater Entrepreneurial School of Technology (MEST): The MEST suite of programs focused on strengthening Ghana’s digital talent pipeline through foundational digital training, startup acceleration, SME scaling, and ecosystem partnerships.

en.title: AAPCRA – Livestock Systems Scoping Study in Ghana and Nigeria
en.description: A livestock ecosystem scoping study commissioned by ACIAR in Ghana and Nigeria, generating evidence for more targeted and effective livestock research and investment.
en.fullDescription: PDA was commissioned by ACIAR to undertake a livestock ecosystem scoping study in Ghana and Nigeria, examining the alignment between the priorities of research institutions, government agencies and development partners and national livestock constraints catalogues, and delivering a final report consolidating findings from the desk review, interviews and stakeholder consultations.
en.snapshot:
**Project Snapshot**

The Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) is the Australian Government's specialist agricultural research-for-development agency, working with public and private research institutions to improve the productivity and sustainability of agricultural systems and contribute to poverty reduction across the Indo-Pacific region.

**PDA's Task**

PDA was commissioned by ACIAR to undertake a livestock ecosystem scoping study in Ghana and Nigeria to generate evidence for more targeted and effective livestock research and investment. The study examined the alignment between the priorities of research institutions, government agencies and development partners and the national livestock constraints catalogues in both countries. It covered the Northern Savannah, Transitional, Humid/Mixed and Coastal zones, with particular attention to species-specific challenges, gender-related constraints and the needs of smallholder farmers.

**How We Went About It**

To deliver the assignment, PDA reviewed relevant project documents and secondary literature, developed qualitative data collection tools, and conducted key informant interviews with stakeholders across Ghana's livestock ecosystem. The team also convened stakeholder co-creation workshops in Ghana's northern and southern belts to review and validate existing evidence, map advisory pathways, identify key actors and highlight gaps in knowledge dissemination. These engagements provided opportunities for stakeholders across the livestock value chain to contribute their perspectives and priorities to the assessment. Similar stakeholder engagement activities were undertaken in Nigeria.

PDA completed the study and submitted the final report to ACIAR, consolidating the findings and insights gathered through the desk review, interviews and stakeholder consultations.

**Impact**

The study provides an evidence base to support the design and delivery of livestock research activities over the subsequent one to three years. By identifying priority constraints, research needs and opportunities for collaboration, the findings can help guide investments that strengthen livestock productivity, resilience and the livelihoods of smallholder farmers in Ghana and Nigeria.

fr.title: AAPCRA – Étude de cadrage des systèmes d'élevage au Ghana et au Nigeria
fr.description: Une étude de cadrage des systèmes d'élevage au Ghana et au Nigeria, commandée par l'ACIAR pour produire des données probantes en faveur d'une recherche et d'un investissement plus ciblés dans le secteur de l'élevage.
fr.fullDescription: Le PDA a été mandaté par l'ACIAR pour mener une étude de cadrage de l'écosystème de l'élevage au Ghana et au Nigeria, examinant l'alignement entre les priorités des institutions de recherche, des agences gouvernementales et des partenaires du développement et les catalogues nationaux des contraintes de l'élevage, et remettant un rapport final consolidant les résultats de la revue documentaire, des entretiens et des consultations des parties prenantes.
fr.snapshot:
**Aperçu du projet**

L'Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) est l'agence spécialisée du gouvernement australien pour la recherche agricole au service du développement, travaillant avec des institutions de recherche publiques et privées pour améliorer la productivité et la durabilité des systèmes agricoles et contribuer à la réduction de la pauvreté dans la région Indo-Pacifique.

**La mission du PDA**

Le PDA a été mandaté par l'ACIAR pour mener une étude de cadrage de l'écosystème de l'élevage au Ghana et au Nigeria, afin de produire des données probantes en faveur d'une recherche et d'un investissement plus ciblés et efficaces dans le secteur de l'élevage. L'étude a examiné l'alignement entre les priorités des institutions de recherche, des agences gouvernementales et des partenaires du développement et les catalogues nationaux des contraintes de l'élevage dans les deux pays. Elle a couvert les zones de savane du Nord, de transition, humide/mixte et côtière, en accordant une attention particulière aux défis spécifiques aux espèces, aux contraintes liées au genre et aux besoins des petits exploitants.

**Comment nous avons procédé**

Pour mener à bien cette mission, le PDA a passé en revue les documents de projet pertinents et la littérature secondaire, élaboré des outils qualitatifs de collecte de données et mené des entretiens avec des informateurs clés auprès des parties prenantes de l'écosystème de l'élevage au Ghana. L'équipe a également organisé des ateliers de co-création avec les parties prenantes dans les zones nord et sud du Ghana afin d'examiner et de valider les données existantes, de cartographier les filières de conseil, d'identifier les acteurs clés et de mettre en évidence les lacunes dans la diffusion des connaissances. Ces échanges ont permis aux parties prenantes de la chaîne de valeur de l'élevage de faire part de leurs points de vue et priorités dans le cadre de l'évaluation. Des activités similaires de mobilisation des parties prenantes ont été menées au Nigeria.

Le PDA a achevé l'étude et soumis le rapport final à l'ACIAR, consolidant les résultats et les constats issus de la revue documentaire, des entretiens et des consultations des parties prenantes.

**Impact**

L'étude fournit une base de données probantes pour appuyer la conception et la mise en œuvre d'activités de recherche sur l'élevage au cours des un à trois prochaines années. En identifiant les contraintes prioritaires, les besoins de recherche et les opportunités de collaboration, les résultats peuvent orienter des investissements qui renforcent la productivité de l'élevage, la résilience et les moyens d'existence des petits exploitants au Ghana et au Nigeria.

en.title: Building Resilient and Active Communities in Extractive Landscapes in Ghana (BRACE)
en.description: A baseline study tracking community resilience and environmental rights outcomes in Ghana's mining regions, commissioned as part of the EU-funded BRACE project.
en.fullDescription: BRACE is a three-year, EU-funded project promoting sustainable environmental management in Ghana's mining regions. PDA was commissioned to design and conduct the project's baseline study, tracking progress and impact across four key work packages.
en.snapshot:
**Project Snapshot**

BRACE is a three-year project funded by the European Union, aimed at promoting sustainable environmental management in mining regions of Ghana. Implemented by A Rocha Ghana in collaboration with Nature Development Foundation and Wacam, the project focuses on enhancing community resilience in the Eastern, Ashanti, Western North, Western, and Ahafo Regions.

**Project Objectives**

Main Goal: Strengthen the capacity of local communities to hold state and private sector actors accountable for environmental rights violations related to extractive activities.
Specific Objectives:
• To build the knowledge, capacity and skills of target groups to hold state and private sector actors to account over violations to communities' environmental human rights, lands, and natural resources by damaging extractive developments
• To provide access to justice systems for local communities whose environmental rights, lands and natural resources have been violated or are threatened by extractive sector activities
• Establish mechanisms for direct engagement between communities and duty bearers to defend their environmental human rights
• Build the capacity of Community Resource Management Area (CREMA) Executive Committees to implement their management plans effectively

**PDA's Task**

Participatory Development Associates (PDA) was commissioned to design and conduct a baseline study to track the progress and impact of the BRACE project, establishing benchmarks against which the project's effectiveness can be measured. The PDA REL team used a cross-sectional mixed-methods approach to gather and analyze data across the project's four key work packages.

**How We Went About It**
• Questionnaire development and scripting of the survey tool, tailored to capture the specific needs and concerns of communities involved in the BRACE project.
• Enumerator recruitment and training: local enumerators who understood community dynamics were recruited and trained to administer the survey and gather accurate, reliable data in the appropriate local languages.
• Field data collection: enumerators conducted fieldwork directly with community members, speaking to 352 sample respondents across the target regions.
• Analysis and reporting: findings were analyzed to identify trends and key insights, producing a detailed report for partners with actionable recommendations for the project's initiatives and advocacy efforts.

**Impact**

The BRACE project targets a range of stakeholders, including 50 community-based organizations, 30 women's groups, 10 civil society organizations, and various traditional authorities, impacting approximately 200 rural communities threatened by mining activities. The insights gained from the baseline study provided critical information to empower community stakeholders and strengthen their advocacy efforts regarding environmental rights.
en.partners: European Union; A Rocha Ghana; Nature Development Foundation; Wacam
en.location: Eastern, Ashanti, Western North, Western and Ahafo Regions, Ghana

fr.title: Renforcement de la résilience des communautés actives dans les paysages extractifs au Ghana (BRACE)
fr.description: Une étude de référence suivant la résilience communautaire et les résultats en matière de droits environnementaux dans les régions minières du Ghana, commandée dans le cadre du projet BRACE financé par l'UE.
fr.fullDescription: BRACE est un projet de trois ans financé par l'Union européenne, promouvant une gestion environnementale durable dans les régions minières du Ghana. Le PDA a été chargé de concevoir et de mener l'étude de référence du projet, suivant les progrès et l'impact à travers quatre volets de travail clés.
fr.snapshot:
**Aperçu du projet**

BRACE est un projet de trois ans financé par l'Union européenne, visant à promouvoir une gestion environnementale durable dans les régions minières du Ghana. Mis en œuvre par A Rocha Ghana en collaboration avec la Nature Development Foundation et Wacam, le projet vise à renforcer la résilience communautaire dans les régions de l'Eastern, de l'Ashanti, du Western North, du Western et de l'Ahafo.

**Objectifs du projet**

Objectif principal : Renforcer la capacité des communautés locales à demander des comptes aux acteurs étatiques et privés concernant les violations des droits environnementaux liées aux activités extractives.
Objectifs spécifiques :
• Développer les connaissances, les capacités et les compétences des groupes cibles pour demander des comptes aux acteurs étatiques et privés concernant les atteintes aux droits humains environnementaux, aux terres et aux ressources naturelles des communautés causées par des aménagements extractifs dommageables ;
• Faciliter l'accès des communautés locales aux systèmes de justice lorsque leurs droits environnementaux, leurs terres et leurs ressources naturelles ont été violés ou sont menacés par les activités du secteur extractif ;
• Mettre en place des mécanismes d'engagement direct entre les communautés et les détenteurs d'obligations pour défendre leurs droits humains environnementaux ;
• Renforcer la capacité des comités exécutifs des zones de gestion des ressources communautaires (CREMA) à mettre en œuvre efficacement leurs plans de gestion.

**La mission du PDA**

Participatory Development Associates (PDA) a été chargé de concevoir et de mener une étude de référence pour suivre les progrès et l'impact du projet BRACE, en établissant des repères permettant de mesurer l'efficacité du projet. L'équipe REL du PDA a utilisé une approche mixte transversale pour collecter et analyser les données à travers les quatre volets de travail clés du projet.

**Comment nous avons procédé**
• Élaboration du questionnaire et scénarisation de l'outil d'enquête, adapté pour saisir les besoins et préoccupations spécifiques des communautés impliquées dans le projet BRACE.
• Recrutement et formation des enquêteurs : des enquêteurs locaux connaissant la dynamique communautaire ont été recrutés et formés pour administrer l'enquête et recueillir des données précises et fiables dans les langues locales appropriées.
• Collecte de données sur le terrain : les enquêteurs ont mené un travail de terrain directement auprès des membres des communautés, s'entretenant avec 352 répondants échantillonnés dans les régions cibles.
• Analyse et rapport : les résultats ont été analysés pour identifier les tendances et les principaux constats, produisant un rapport détaillé pour les partenaires avec des recommandations concrètes pour les initiatives du projet et les efforts de plaidoyer.

**Impact**

Le projet BRACE cible un éventail de parties prenantes, notamment 50 organisations communautaires, 30 groupes de femmes, 10 organisations de la société civile et diverses autorités traditionnelles, touchant environ 200 communautés rurales menacées par les activités minières. Les constats de l'étude de référence ont fourni des informations essentielles pour renforcer l'autonomisation des parties prenantes communautaires et consolider leurs efforts de plaidoyer en matière de droits environnementaux.
fr.partners: Union européenne ; A Rocha Ghana ; Nature Development Foundation ; Wacam

en.title: SDG Kids
en.description: A child-centred participatory programme building children's awareness of the Sustainable Development Goals and their capacity to lead action towards them in their communities.
en.fullDescription: SDG Kids promotes awareness of the Sustainable Development Goals among children and young people, using child-centred participatory methodologies and interactive activities to build their capacity to take action in support of the SDGs by 2030.
en.snapshot:
**Project Snapshot**

SDG Kids is a project which focuses on promoting awareness of the Sustainable Development Goals among children and young people. The project uses child-centred participatory methodologies and interactive activities to help build children's capacity to take action in support of the attainment of the SDGs by 2030.

**Project Objectives**
The goal of the SDG Kids project is to harness the potential of children and young people to initiate actions in their communities and contribute towards implementation of the SDGs by 2030.
1. To enable young people to develop understanding and awareness of the Sustainable Development Goals.
2. To facilitate processes that enable children and young people to become agents of change and initiate their own projects promoting development in their communities.
3. To help children and young people in their personal development (leadership).

**Implementation Approach**
• Formation of SDG Action Clubs in communities to take action and lead SDG Kids' project activities in schools.
• Engagement of children through games, arts, crafts and competitions in addressing developmental challenges in their communities.
• Children-community engagement events.

**Expected Outcomes**
• Children in communities gain full knowledge and understanding of the Sustainable Development Goals.
• Children become agents of change in their communities, leading and implementing their own projects.
• Communities involve children in community decision-making and implementation processes.

**Aperçu du projet**

SDG Kids est un projet axé sur la sensibilisation des enfants et des jeunes aux Objectifs de développement durable. Le projet utilise des méthodologies participatives centrées sur l'enfant et des activités interactives pour aider à renforcer la capacité des enfants à agir en faveur de l'atteinte des ODD d'ici 2030.

**Objectifs du projet**
L'objectif de SDG Kids est d'exploiter le potentiel des enfants et des jeunes pour qu'ils initient des actions dans leurs communautés et contribuent à la mise en œuvre des ODD d'ici 2030.
1. Permettre aux jeunes de développer leur compréhension et leur connaissance des Objectifs de développement durable.
2. Faciliter des processus permettant aux enfants et aux jeunes de devenir des agents de changement et d'initier leurs propres projets de développement dans leurs communautés.
3. Accompagner le développement personnel (leadership) des enfants et des jeunes.

**Approche de mise en œuvre**
• Création de clubs d'action ODD dans les communautés pour mener les activités du projet SDG Kids dans les écoles.
• Engagement des enfants par le biais de jeux, d'arts, d'artisanat et de concours pour relever les défis de développement de leurs communautés.
• Événements de mobilisation enfants-communauté.

**Résultats attendus**
• Les enfants des communautés acquièrent une pleine connaissance et compréhension des Objectifs de développement durable.
• Les enfants deviennent des agents de changement dans leurs communautés, en dirigeant et en mettant en œuvre leurs propres projets.
• Les communautés impliquent les enfants dans les processus décisionnels et de mise en œuvre communautaires.

en.title: The Cocoa Nutrition Innovation Project
en.description: A behavioural change communications pilot improving dietary diversity and hygiene practices in cocoa-growing households, monitored and evaluated by PDA.
en.fullDescription: The Cocoa Nutrition Innovation (CNI) Project, led by the Sustainable Trade Initiative (IDH) and Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN), used a behavioural change communications strategy to improve dietary diversity and hand-washing practices in cocoa-growing households, with PDA providing monitoring and evaluation consultancy.
en.snapshot:
**Project Snapshot**

The Cocoa Nutrition Innovation (CNI) Project is an intervention by the Sustainable Trade Initiative (IDH) and Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN), which aimed to improve the nutritional status of households in cocoa-growing communities. The CNI is a behavioural change communications (BCC) strategy aimed at effecting change in dietary diversity and hand-washing practices, piloted in Ghana based on the successful Kenyan version, Seeds of Prosperity.

The project was based on the premise that even though nutritious foods are often available and accessible in rural farming communities, many families are not aware of the importance of a nutritious diet. A BCC campaign strategy was developed focusing on dietary diversity, cooking practices, hand washing and hygiene — encouraging participants to eat at least five of ten food groups daily and wash their hands five times daily.

**Project Components**
• Behavioural change communication nutrition training.
• Seed provision, animal rearing inputs and related training activities.
• Monitoring and evaluation of project activities.

Three implementing organisations — Lindt, Touton and Hershey — provided nine weeks of training in five districts: Ataase, New Edubiase, Assin Fosu, Tepa and Goaso. The training focused on women of cocoa farming households, since they are mostly responsible for food choices in the household.

**PDA's Task**
PDA provided monitoring and evaluation consultancy services for the CNI with the objectives of:
• Assessing fidelity of the training to training plans.
• Critiquing and offering recommendations for replicability.
• Assessing the project's impact on nutritional and personal hygiene behaviours.

Apart from progress evaluation, PDA also undertook a summative evaluation at the end of the project, using the 4-levels of the Kirkpatrick evaluation framework for analysis. Participatory tools such as focus group discussions, exit interviews and in-depth interviews complemented training observations across all five districts, measuring change in knowledge, attitudes and practices around nutrition and hygiene over the course of the programme.
en.partners: Sustainable Trade Initiative (IDH); Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN); Lindt; Touton; Hershey
en.location: Ataase, New Edubiase, Assin Fosu, Tepa and Goaso, Ghana

fr.title: Le projet d'innovation en nutrition cacaoyère
fr.description: Un projet pilote de communication pour le changement de comportement améliorant la diversité alimentaire et les pratiques d'hygiène dans les ménages cacaoyers, suivi et évalué par le PDA.
fr.fullDescription: Le projet d'innovation en nutrition cacaoyère (CNI), piloté par la Sustainable Trade Initiative (IDH) et la Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN), a utilisé une stratégie de communication pour le changement de comportement afin d'améliorer la diversité alimentaire et les pratiques de lavage des mains dans les ménages cacaoyers, le PDA assurant le conseil en suivi-évaluation.
fr.snapshot:
**Aperçu du projet**

Le projet d'innovation en nutrition cacaoyère (CNI) est une intervention de la Sustainable Trade Initiative (IDH) et de la Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN), visant à améliorer l'état nutritionnel des ménages dans les communautés cacaoyères. Le CNI est une stratégie de communication pour le changement de comportement (CCC) visant à faire évoluer la diversité alimentaire et les pratiques de lavage des mains, pilotée au Ghana sur la base de la version kényane réussie, Seeds of Prosperity.

Le projet repose sur le constat que, même si des aliments nutritifs sont souvent disponibles et accessibles dans les communautés agricoles rurales, de nombreuses familles ne sont pas conscientes de l'importance d'une alimentation nutritive. Une stratégie de campagne CCC a été élaborée, axée sur la diversité alimentaire, les pratiques culinaires, le lavage des mains et l'hygiène — encourageant les participants à consommer au moins cinq des dix groupes alimentaires chaque jour et à se laver les mains cinq fois par jour.

**Composantes du projet**
• Formation en communication pour le changement de comportement nutritionnel.
• Fourniture de semences, d'intrants d'élevage et activités de formation associées.
• Suivi et évaluation des activités du projet.

Trois organisations de mise en œuvre — Lindt, Touton et Hershey — ont assuré neuf semaines de formation dans cinq districts : Ataase, New Edubiase, Assin Fosu, Tepa et Goaso. La formation ciblait les femmes des ménages cacaoyers, car elles sont majoritairement responsables des choix alimentaires au sein du foyer.

**La mission du PDA**
Le PDA a fourni des services de conseil en suivi-évaluation pour le CNI avec les objectifs suivants :
• Évaluer la fidélité de la formation par rapport aux plans de formation.
• Analyser de façon critique et formuler des recommandations pour la réplicabilité.
• Évaluer l'impact du projet sur les comportements nutritionnels et d'hygiène personnelle.

Au-delà de l'évaluation des progrès, le PDA a également mené une évaluation sommative à la fin du projet, en utilisant les 4 niveaux du cadre d'évaluation de Kirkpatrick pour l'analyse. Des outils participatifs tels que des discussions de groupe, des entretiens de sortie et des entretiens approfondis ont complété les observations de formation dans les cinq districts, mesurant l'évolution des connaissances, attitudes et pratiques en matière de nutrition et d'hygiène tout au long du programme.

fr.location: Ataase, New Edubiase, Assin Fosu, Tepa et Goaso, Ghana

en.title: Vulnerability and Exclusion Assessment for UNICEF Ghana and the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection
en.description: A study supporting UNICEF Ghana and the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection to adopt a consistent working definition of vulnerability and exclusion for the Ghanaian context.
en.fullDescription: PDA, in partnership with the Overseas Development Institute (ODI), conducted a Vulnerability and Exclusion assessment study to help the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP) and UNICEF Ghana adopt a suitable working definition of vulnerability and exclusion for the Ghanaian context.

**Project Snapshot**

en.title: Impact Study of Rainforest Alliance Certification for Cashew Farmers in Benin and Côte d'Ivoire
en.description: An assessment of the early outcomes of Rainforest Alliance certification for cashew farmers under the Move Com-Cashew Program, examining incomes, climate resilience, employment and women's participation.
en.fullDescription: PDA is conducting an impact study of Rainforest Alliance certification under the GIZ-funded, ETG Commodities BV-implemented Move Com-Cashew Program, assessing how certification is influencing cashew production, farmer incomes, climate resilience, employment, market access and women's participation in Benin and Côte d'Ivoire.
en.snapshot:
**Project Snapshot**

The Move Com-Cashew Program, funded by GIZ and implemented by ETG Commodities BV, aims to strengthen the competitiveness of the cashew value chain in West Africa. The programme supports capacity-building in Good Agricultural Practices (GAP), strengthens farmer cooperatives, promotes local processing capacity and employment creation, and encourages innovation in the use of cashew apples to produce products such as juice, animal feed and cosmetics. It targets 5,000 cashew farmers in Benin and Côte d'Ivoire, with women accounting for 50% of the target group. A key component is the introduction and scale-up of Rainforest Alliance (RA) certification within the cashew sector.

**PDA's Task**

PDA is conducting an impact study to assess the early outcomes of RA certification and the support activities accompanying its implementation. The study examines how certification is influencing cashew production, farmer incomes, climate resilience, employment and access to markets, as well as the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices and certification requirements.

The assessment also explores farmers' awareness of labour practices, occupational health and safety, and governance within producer groups. Particular attention is given to the factors enabling or limiting women's participation in training, group leadership, certification processes and market access. In addition, the study examines the quality of implementation, identifying what is working well, what requires adjustment and the conditions needed to support wider adoption.

**How We Went About It**

As part of the assignment, PDA officers conducted a two-day training workshop in Benin for ETG enumerators to prepare them for data collection among cashew farmers. This capacity-building support helps equip the field team to implement the study and gather relevant evidence on farmers' experiences with Rainforest Alliance certification.

**Impact**

Through this study, PDA is generating evidence to inform programme decision-making, strengthen implementation and guide the potential scale-up of Rainforest Alliance certification in the West African cashew sector.

fr.title: Étude d'impact de la certification Rainforest Alliance pour les producteurs d'anacarde au Bénin et en Côte d'Ivoire
fr.description: Une évaluation des premiers résultats de la certification Rainforest Alliance pour les producteurs d'anacarde dans le cadre du programme Move Com-Cashew, portant sur les revenus, la résilience climatique, l'emploi et la participation des femmes.
fr.fullDescription: Le PDA mène une étude d'impact de la certification Rainforest Alliance dans le cadre du programme Move Com-Cashew, financé par la GIZ et mis en œuvre par ETG Commodities BV, évaluant comment la certification influence la production d'anacarde, les revenus des producteurs, la résilience climatique, l'emploi, l'accès aux marchés et la participation des femmes au Bénin et en Côte d'Ivoire.
fr.snapshot:
**Aperçu du projet**

Le programme Move Com-Cashew, financé par la GIZ et mis en œuvre par ETG Commodities BV, vise à renforcer la compétitivité de la chaîne de valeur de l'anacarde en Afrique de l'Ouest. Le programme appuie le renforcement des capacités en bonnes pratiques agricoles (BPA), renforce les coopératives d'agriculteurs, favorise la capacité de transformation locale et la création d'emplois, et encourage l'innovation dans l'utilisation des pommes de cajou pour produire des produits tels que du jus, des aliments pour animaux et des cosmétiques. Il cible 5 000 producteurs d'anacarde au Bénin et en Côte d'Ivoire, les femmes représentant 50 % du groupe cible. Une composante clé est l'introduction et la mise à l'échelle de la certification Rainforest Alliance (RA) dans le secteur de l'anacarde.

**La mission du PDA**

Le PDA mène une étude d'impact pour évaluer les premiers résultats de la certification RA et des activités d'accompagnement de sa mise en œuvre. L'étude examine comment la certification influence la production d'anacarde, les revenus des producteurs, la résilience climatique, l'emploi et l'accès aux marchés, ainsi que l'adoption de pratiques agricoles durables et des exigences de certification.

L'évaluation explore également la connaissance qu'ont les producteurs des pratiques de travail, de la santé et de la sécurité au travail, et de la gouvernance au sein des groupes de producteurs. Une attention particulière est accordée aux facteurs favorisant ou limitant la participation des femmes à la formation, à la direction des groupes, aux processus de certification et à l'accès aux marchés. En outre, l'étude examine la qualité de la mise en œuvre, en identifiant ce qui fonctionne bien, ce qui nécessite des ajustements et les conditions nécessaires pour appuyer une adoption plus large.

**Comment nous avons procédé**

Dans le cadre de cette mission, des agents du PDA ont animé un atelier de formation de deux jours au Bénin pour les enquêteurs d'ETG, afin de les préparer à la collecte de données auprès des producteurs d'anacarde. Cet appui au renforcement des capacités aide à équiper l'équipe de terrain pour mener l'étude et recueillir des données pertinentes sur l'expérience des producteurs avec la certification Rainforest Alliance.

**Impact**

Grâce à cette étude, le PDA produit des données probantes pour éclairer la prise de décision du programme, renforcer la mise en œuvre et orienter la mise à l'échelle potentielle de la certification Rainforest Alliance dans le secteur de l'anacarde en Afrique de l'Ouest.
